rgb: Viewed from a sharply downward egocentric angle, the scene shows an outdoor grassy lawn with nobody present except the camera wearer. At 0 to 0.5 metres directly beneath the viewpoint are the wearer’s grey shirt, shoulders, and chin. Both arms reach forward and downward, with the hands holding a lawnmower handlebar approximately 0.5 to 0.6 metres away. From the handlebar at 0.5 metres, the walk-behind mower projects ahead to its grey grass-catcher bag at around 0.8 to 1.1 metres, then to the silver deck and red engine housing at roughly 1.1 to 1.5 metres; the top of every frame partly crops the mower deck’s front edge. Both hands hold the bar comfortably within arm’s reach, and the grass-catcher bag immediately ahead of the wearer’s legs is also reachable. The wearer’s torso and handlebar partly block the black shorts, legs, and alternating shoes directly below, while the mower conceals the grass underneath its body. Throughout the five frames, wearer and mower preserve almost the same spacing and alignment, remaining about 0.5 to 1.5 metres apart as they move forward together across the lawn with minor side-to-side shifts and alternating foot placements.
depth: Across five frames, the depth map presents a steeply downward egocentric view of an outdoor lawn as the camera wearer—the sole person in the scene, facing ahead while looking directly downward—pushes a walk-behind lawn mower. White and pale-grey shading locates the wearer’s upper torso 0.1–0.4 m beneath the head-mounted camera, the two outstretched arms and hands grasping the handlebar within reach about 0.5–0.7 m forward and below, and the mower’s grass-catcher bag and engine deck farther ahead at ground level, approximately 1.0–1.7 m from the camera and 0.5–1.0 m beyond the handlebar. In the space between the occluding torso and handlebar, somewhat darker-grey forms alternate by frame: the left leg/foot appears in frames 1, 2, and 5, both knees/feet in frame 3, and the right leg in frame 4. These occur 0.8–1.4 m below the camera as the wearer advances while keeping a fixed distance from the mower, whose front edge is partially cropped along the frame’s top. Relative to RGB, depth clearly distinguishes the vertical height transition from the elevated handlebar, along its sloping support rods, to the mower body and ground plane, without confusion from patchy grass and mulch textures. Still, thin lateral cables/rods are unreliable and partly disappear into the dark ground depth, while gentle slopes in the flat grassy background are compressed into nearly uniform black.
segmentation: Against the unlabelled black lawn background, the segmentation map separates the camera wearer’s torso, arms, hands, and walking legs at bottom center, 0.1–1.4 m from the camera; the wearer faces forward and looks downward, and no one else is present. In every one of the five frames, the left and right hands grip the mower handlebar immediately ahead of the torso at 0.5–0.7 m, within arm’s reach. The torso hides most of the lower body, leaving it visible mainly through the opening between the arms and bar. While the wearer proceeds forward with mild side-to-side sway and turns slightly left by frame 5, the mask records changes in the opening’s shape between the arms and chest, where the stepping legs and handlebar appear; meanwhile, both the mower’s top and the bottom of the wearer’s head remain partly outside the view. The mask reveals the continuous outline of the upper body and arms more clearly than RGB, but semantic labelling and object detection are very unreliable from this steep egocentric perspective. It omits the lawn mower entirely in frames 2, 3, and 5; in frames 1 and 4, it wrongly identifies the mower deck and grass bag about 1.0–1.7 m ahead as a “parking meter” plus a tiny “person” fragment. It also absorbs the handlebar into the “person” mask in frames 2–3 and labels the bar’s center as a “cell phone” in frame 5.
pose: On a black background, the pose map displays only two magenta 2D hand skeletons, representing the camera wearer’s left and right hands within reach approximately 0.5–0.7 m forward and below the downward-facing camera. The hands are separated horizontally by about 0.3–0.4 m along the lawnmower handlebar. For each skeleton, the wrist lies at the outer lower corner, and all five fingers curl forward and inward around the slanted grips. This confirms that the wearer stands facing forward behind the mower and that no other people occupy the scene. Over the five frames, both hand skeletons move slightly higher in frames 2–3; in frame 5, the pair rotates a little counter-clockwise, leaving the left hand higher and the right hand lower. These changes follow the subtle angle of the handlebar and the wearer’s torso sway during forward walking. In comparison with RGB, the magenta keypoints clearly expose precise finger articulation, thumb position, and the grip’s symmetrical orientation without interference from the grass or handlebar. Nevertheless, the map is unreliable for understanding the whole body: it entirely misses the yellow body skeleton for the visible shoulders, elbows, torso, and stepping legs, which are strongly foreshortened and self-occluded by the head-mounted viewing angle, and it depicts neither the lawn mower nor the ground.
